title: Atlas documents are editable through the Weekly Cycle only if they explicitly say they are
content:
A.1.11.1.1 restricts the fast lane: "The Operational Weekly Cycle may be used to edit the Atlas only if the pertinent Atlas document specifies that it, or a related unit of governance logic which it expressly controls, is modifiable through the Operational Weekly Cycle."

The structure is opt-in with a strict default. Where a document does grant weekly amendability, "an Operational Weekly Cycle proposal requires a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote" — and that general rule "is assumed wherever the Atlas provides" weekly modifiability. Anything lighter must be spelled out: the enumerated exceptions are Poll-only, and Executive-only without a prior Poll.

Two defaults are therefore doing the work. Silence about the cycle means *not weekly-editable at all*, and silence about the process within a weekly-editable document means *the full two-step*. Both defaults fail closed, so a drafting omission can never accidentally create a cheap path to amending the Atlas.

This is the counterpart to the Weekly Cycle's purpose stated in A.1.11.1 — enabling "recurring weekly decisions to be made that require quicker action than is allowed by the Monthly Governance Cycle." Speed is made available deliberately and per-document, rather than as an ambient option that proposers can reach for.
description: Weekly-cycle amendability is opt-in per document; where granted, Poll-then-Executive is the default, and any lighter path must be stated in that document.
